dynein and Ndc80, two protein complexes that are required for kinetochore attachment, inhibit each other's binding to microtubules and that this crosstalk is required for proper chromosome segregation.
the microtubule motor complex dynein and the microtubul binding protein complex NDC80 are both important for chromosome segregation.

the molecular basis of chromosome segregation.

the mechanisms by which the kinetochores of chromosomes establish stable attachments to the mitotic spindle during cell division, and the role of this process in ensuring accurate chromosome segregation.
chromosome segregation, a fundamental process that is critical for the maintenance of genome stability and the fidelity of cell division.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the kinetochores have to be able to regulate the formation of microtubule-kinetochore attachments in a very dynamic fashion, and they do that through the regulation of the two major protein machines involved in forming those attachments: the Ndc80 and dynein complexes.
